entry_state: The capped-participation allocation recalculates class earnings after assumed issuance and supports ordering only for complete additive gross effects. A shared bonus and tax schedule makes conversion effects nonadditive, so correct hypothetical worlds do not themselves settle admissible dilution selection. A contingent-option example now introduces the separate requirement to assume similar outstanding instruments; its calculation continues next.
exit_state: Contingent options require both the period-end condition and the applicable similar-instrument prerequisite. Participating dividends can alter the ordinary EPS numerator through a hypothetical tax benefit, including a signed reversal when older profits are paid. These allocations create no journal. The chapter now introduces a dated control graph and separate consolidation adjustment book, followed by the more detailed perimeter method.
findings: The contingent-option examples enforce the similar-instrument prerequisite even when the contingent series alone would reduce EPS.
The participating-tax derivation preserves negative residual allocations without inventing a cash dividend or tax asset, and proves payout timing cancels under fixed rights.
The manuscript explicitly allows class EPS allocations to exceed reported profit because of the hypothetical tax consequence, without posting that difference.
The simple consolidation illustration is labeled as a different acquisition from the later goodwill case. No new confirmed local defect.
